finding:
Printed claim. For a number field and fixed norm-one isotype with the half twist, I=[−a,a], a>0 arbitrary, and φ a compact smooth test supported over norm >1+ε for some ε>0, let A be the operator on the completed Hilbert quotient induced by the unnumbered convolution display on p. 14 immediately above ‘on S_E’. At s=0 the unnumbered expansion on p. 14 takes every interior zero ρ of L(s,χ) in the shifted coordinate z=ρ−1/2, with all orders 0≤m<N(ρ). The rank-one term sends u to (A′ℓρ,m)(u) ψρ,m, with transpose A′ℓ=ℓ∘A and ψρ,m the image of the original Fréchet biorthogonal vector, not an independently chosen vector from an orthonormal basis. The printed ordering is by increasing |Im ρ| of zero blocks, and the asserted limit is A in trace norm. Use full height cutoffs |Im ρ|≤T, including ties, for the cutoff formulation; if using individual prefixes of a chosen tied ordering, those prefixes must also be controlled. The kernel representation following this is not the claim audited here. The positive-s branch additionally invokes the p. 13 boundary count max{N(ρ),[(s−1)/2]}; this is not the minimum in (10.2.2.5) and need not respect the strict continuity requirement 2m+1<s (already m=0 fails if 0<s≤1 and there is a retained boundary zero). The rational necessary threshold is checked by Masullo.rationalRadialQuotient_boundaryJet_lt in Proofs/Theorems/RationalRadialBoundaryJet.lean. This boundary issue does not explain away the s=0 interior gap.

Source argument and first missing bridges. Thm. 7.1.4.2(3) gives the original all-zero Fréchet biorthogonals; its proof divides the entire completed divisor by (s−ρ)^(N(ρ)−m) and makes a finite triangular change within each zero to get exact derivative pairings, not Hilbert norm estimates. The strong nuclearity result referred to on p. 452, Thm. 7.4.1.1(2), concerns a Fréchet subspace with a fixed cap N on jet orders, not all interior orders or the specified Hilbert trace-norm limit. The fixed-coordinate half twist reindexes the Mellin exponent by 1/2. A separate representative comparison is needed to infer ℓρ,m(ψσ,k)=δρσδmk in the completed quotient: the ambient extended shifted jet must annihilate the actual closed theta range, and the continuous pairing must agree with the original Fréchet pairing on projected representatives. Theorem 10.2.2.1 claims a Hilbert Markushevich system. Its cited (9.3.2.10) is an intersection of kernels that shrinks as the cutoff grows, not an increasing subspace with projectors tending strongly to identity by the printed argument. Orthogonal projectors onto orthogonal complements of the joint kernels, if totality has been independently established on the actual quotient, are increasing, but are not the prescribed coordinate projectors.

Finite blocks versus their limit. Conditionally on the representative/biorthogonality bridge, define P_T u=Σψρ,m ℓρ,m(u) over the full retained blocks. The printed finite sum is P_T A, with P_T in general oblique. In raw derivative coordinates the m-th transpose row at z is Σ_{k=0}^m binom(m,k) (∂_z^(m−k) M(φ))(z) ℓρ,k; no cap below N(ρ) for interior zeros. Taylor normalization divides each jet by m! and rescales its paired vector by m!, leaving the rank-one terms unchanged. The finite block trace is N(ρ)M(φ)(z) with the fixed character implicit; the matrix is invertible exactly when the common diagonal is nonzero (full rank does not follow from multiplicity). If a trace-norm limit exists, evaluation by any fixed jet agrees exactly, once that block is retained, with that jet applied to A. Continuity and separation of points then identify the limit with A. This gives no Cauchy estimate.

Unsupported norm inference. Theorem 10.3.2.1 assumes s>1, not s=0; its statement (1) says Schatten p≥1, while the closing proof on p. 455 invokes p>1 summability and carries over the singleton-base argument. That argument needs a uniform bound on products of jet norms and biorthogonal-vector norms in (10.3.1.18). The annulus bound on jets and the ‘regular’ inference of Terminology 10.2.1.2 do not supply it: biorthogonality implies 1≤‖ℓ‖‖ψ‖, not an upper bound. For a check of the inference, on the Hilbert direct sum of copies of ℂ² let the two functionals per copy be x and x+ε_n y, with ε_n=c_n², c_n=2^(−n), n≥1. Their biorthogonals in that copy are (1,−1/ε_n) and (0,1/ε_n); the functionals are total and uniformly bounded above and away from zero, and the vectors span a dense subspace. Take the trace-class A=⊕c_n Id₂. Label the two functionals at successive distinct heights 2n and 2n+1 as singleton blocks. A cutoff through 2n has compression to copy n of trace norm c_n√(1+ε_n^(−2)), unbounded, even though the diagonal sum is absolutely convergent. This tests the proof inference only, not the actual Hecke jet system or convolution.

retry: First prove for each full interior rational jet at s=0, after the exact weighted-coordinate isometry, that it annihilates every rationalRadialThetaToHilbert input, not just the unramified tensors. One concrete test is to use the accepted finite-unit averaging, decompose each invariant stage into rational finite-ball indicators via valuation strata and rescale onto the unit ball to obtain a real Schwartz lattice representative with the same class theta and both zero modes (or prove direct Mellin divisibility for every original input). Then descend by the actual closed kernel and check the jet values on images of original biorthogonals using the same shift and normalization. To retry the expansion itself, supply a trace-norm Cauchy bound for the actual whole interior blocks along the absolute-ordinate cutoffs, including all orders through N(ρ)−1 and the Hilbert norms of the lifted vectors. For example, a summable majorant for ‖Σ_m ψρ,m⊗(ℓρ,m∘A)‖₁, where the tensor denotes the displayed rank-one action, suffices; coefficient decay alone does not. Finally establish that the retained jets separate the actual separated completion (closed theta range equals their joint kernel in the ambient Hilbert space), or separately show the trace-norm limit equals A on a dense subspace. A rational result is only a specialization of the fixed-isotype, arbitrary-field claim; any positive-s treatment must also reconcile the printed boundary rule with continuous descent.
